title: The Distance Rule That Makes Tides Strong

segments.text: Tidal force grows with Earth's diameter and shrinks with distance cubed.
Gravitational pull falls with distance squared, but tides care about the slope, which falls with distance cubed.
A steeper slope means a larger difference between near and far sides.
The Moon’s pull declines more steeply across Earth than the Sun’s.
That steep gradient produces the larger bulge.
The slope wins over total pull.
The rule explains why closeness matters.
